title: Brava Security report: exposed log collectors accepted fabricated security events
date_note: SiliconANGLE and the report are dated 24 Nov 2026; no earlier day given.
summary: According to SiliconANGLE's account of Brava Security's 'Ghost Feeds' report, internet-exposed log collectors accepted fabricated security events without credentials, which could let attackers tamper with breach evidence. Brava also released a free open-source tool, ghost-telemetry-check, to test whether a logging pipeline accepts unauthenticated events.
plain: Researchers at Brava Security say many exposed logging systems accept fake security events with no login, which could hide or muddy evidence of a breach.
exec: Per Brava Security, unauthenticated log collectors could let attackers plant false events; the firm offers a free test tool.
action: Brava Security advises testing pipelines with its free open-source ghost-telemetry-check tool, which checks whether a logging pipeline accepts unauthenticated events.

validation.note: Only SiliconANGLE's article was read; Brava's own report was not opened.

review.note: Removed unsupported absence claim about vendor statements; not on the page
